drafted_from: tool:keep-a-facebook-pages-token's row in tools/connect-a-service-and-seal-its-key/tool-rows.json (job, description, input_schema, invoke) and the folder's test/connect-by-signing-in.test.mjs, whose stand-in answers give the reply and the held word
start_here: Say to your AI: "Keep one Facebook Page's token for the new connection service_connection:facebook-messenger:7d3c88e1 with the code made-up-code-4f9a2c." It runs tool:keep-a-facebook-pages-token and tells you the tokens are kept in the vault without showing any of them.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it sends one request to Facebook for the connection it is handed and keeps the tokens in the vault as that connection's fields.
instructions: 1. Do not run this by hand: tool:connect-an-account-by-signing-in-to-the-service runs it for you at the sign-in callback, after you open the sign-in address it gave you. Start that tool first (its kit shows the call) and keep the connection_id it answers: service_connection:facebook-messenger:7d3c88e1 is the shape.

2. To run this step alone, the AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:keep-a-facebook-pages-token and the input the worked example shows (the connection by its handle only, and the Page id chosen from the list step).
3. Read what comes back: the service's reply with every kept token already replaced by the word [held]. The Page's own token now sits in the vault as the connection's page_access_token field.
4. A refusal (a used-up code, a wrong callback address) is shown as the service's own error; nothing is kept, so start the sign-in again for a new link.

worked_examples.title: Keep one Facebook Page's token for a made-up connection
worked_examples.ask: Keep one Facebook Page's token for service_connection:facebook-messenger:7d3c88e1.
worked_examples.given: From tools/connect-a-service-and-seal-its-key/test/connect-by-signing-in.test.mjs (its stand-in for this tool's answer, made up the way the engine answers: every token is already the held word "[held]", because reply_holds_values keeps each token in the vault before the reply is read); the row asks graph.facebook.com/v23.0/{page_id}?fields=access_token with the held user token, and the test's twoPages case runs it with page_id 1000000000000002. Input: {"connection":{"connection_id":"service_connection:facebook-messenger:7d3c88e1"},"page_id":"1000000000000002"}.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"id":"1000000000000002","access_token":"[held]"}. The Page's own token now sits in the vault as the connection's page_access_token field.
